relationships.description: The application's router configuration groups the breadcrumb configuration that derives the location trail for its routes, while that configuration remains a separately defined object that could be shared or reused.
relationships.evidence: The root router setup imports or registers a breadcrumb configuration object, such as a breadcrumb provider or a shared breadcrumb options module, that is defined outside the route table file.

relationships.description: The application's complete route table includes each named multi-step journey, such as checkout or onboarding, as a grouping of its routes, while the flow definition stays an independently defined unit.
relationships.evidence: A flow or wizard definition module, such as a checkout step list or a nested router with ordered child steps, is imported into and mounted within the application's root router configuration.

relationships.description: The application router collects the interceptor hooks registered against it (global, per-route or per-flow), and each guard remains a standalone function or class that could also be attached elsewhere.
relationships.evidence: The router instance registers the guard, for example via router.beforeEach(authGuard) or canActivate: [AuthGuard] entries that reference guard classes defined in separate files.

relationships.description: The application's router configuration gathers every permitted route-to-route move, such as links, redirects and programmatic navigations, into its overall navigation graph.
relationships.evidence: Redirect entries in the route table, router.navigate/push calls, and link components that target routes declared in the same router instance enumerate the edges between its routes.

relationships.description: The application's top-level router holds each route entry in its table, where routes may be defined in separate feature modules and merged into the graph.
relationships.evidence: Feature-module route arrays, such as imported child routes or loadChildren modules, are spread or mounted into the root createRouter/RouterModule.forRoot route list.

relationships.description: Each permitted route change exists only within the application's router configuration that defines both its source and destination routes, so it has no meaning outside that graph.
relationships.evidence: The redirect or navigation edge is declared inline in the root router's route table, for example a redirectTo or redirect property, and is removed when that router configuration is removed.

relationships.description: Each route entry is an integral part of the application's single router configuration and ceases to exist as a matchable path when that router instance is torn down.
relationships.evidence: The route object literal is declared directly in the routes array passed to the application's createRouter, RouterModule.forRoot, or createBrowserRouter call.

relationships.description: The application's router configuration relies on platform software, such as the browser runtime, the JavaScript engine, or the web server that serves history-mode fallbacks, to resolve URLs and execute navigation.
relationships.evidence: The package manifest pins the router library and runtime version, or the web server/CDN configuration (e.g. nginx try_files to index.html) supports the router's history mode.

notes: Aggregates and composes are both defined for Route and NavigationTransition, which gives contradictory lifecycle semantics for the same pair; keep one per pair, preferably composes for Route and NavigationTransition. The uses→SystemSoftware relationship is weak, because a front-end route table depends mainly on a router library or the browser rather than on host system software.
